expectedEvidence.statement: Student records each entry with its status and keeps status separate from any conclusion about a component.
expectedEvidence.notes: Stored and pending must not be collapsed into a single 'fault' statement.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student states that a stored entry is evidence of a monitored condition and does not by itself prove a component failed.
expectedEvidence.notes: This is the core objective of the week.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student distinguishes which interpretation depends on a generic code definition and which would require a manufacturer-specific definition that is unavailable here.
expectedEvidence.notes: Accept 'cannot be determined from the supplied information' as correct.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student states the operating window indicated by the freeze-frame conditions and states what it does not establish.
expectedEvidence.notes: Freeze frame constrains when the condition occurred, not which component caused it.

expectedEvidence.statement: Student states that clearing codes is not acceptable as repair verification on its own.

acceptableAlternatives.statement: Any independently justified measurement plan is acceptable if it names a decision point.
acceptableAlternatives.notes: Do not require a specific measurement or a specific component.

acceptableAlternatives.statement: Students may conclude that neither hypothesis can be separated with the supplied evidence, provided they state what evidence would separate them.
acceptableAlternatives.notes: This is a strong answer, not an evasion.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: A stored code proves the component has failed.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: A stored code records that a monitored condition was detected. Ask the student to separate the detection from a component conclusion and to name the missing evidence.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: Freeze frame identifies the faulty part.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: Freeze frame describes the conditions at capture. Ask what it does and does not narrow.

misconceptionFeedback.misconception: Clearing the code and seeing it stay off verifies the repair.
misconceptionFeedback.feedback: Clearing removes the record, not the cause, and some monitors require a full drive cycle. Ask what independent evidence would be needed.

debriefPrompts: Which part of your interpretation depended on a definition you could not verify?
What evidence would separate your two hypotheses?

sources.title: Project-authored Week 4 instructor evidence guide
sources.notes: Authored for this repository. Contains no real diagnostic trouble code definition.

sources.title: Source-governed OBD-I/OBD-II reference catalog (PR #1063, unmerged)
sources.notes: Instructors must not substitute unverified generic or manufacturer-specific definitions.

technicalReviewChecklist.statement: Guide asserts no real code definition, OEM threshold or monitor result.
Expected evidence is reachable without a verified code definition.
Feedback keeps status, capture conditions and component conclusions separate.
No answer content appears in the student bundle.
